minutes.headline: Board set 90-day earth removal permit renewals, adopted white Town Hall paint, and heard heated town center debate.
minutes.summary: Public comment and board remarks centered on rumors about reusing the TC Passios building for town offices and the old primary site. The board renewed earth removal permits for 90 days, approved a toll drive, liquor and entertainment licenses, Lions Club signs, white Town Hall paint, a larger trash bag pilot, a T-Mobile occupancy license, and a new manager evaluation form (one member opposed). It then went into executive session on litigation.

public_comment.topic: Objected to implication she was behind Facebook comments; argued people may disagree about the town center and TCP move, and raised concerns about selling and municipal identity.
Same speaker continued: concerns about leaving town center, asbestos, TCP condition, TAPA study scope, Town Hall's revenue not being mentioned, open space.
Disheartened that opposition to moving town offices to the TCP seems belittled; asked where residents can be heard respectfully.
Said volunteers include residents and claimed she was slandered during the campaign.

what_happened.line: The Select Board renewed three earth removal permits for 90 days with no new fee if extended; the Montori vote passed, and the Keating and Powell votes were not audible.
The board will send a letter listing which permits are considered inactive and will schedule a follow-up hearing and a public discussion of closure standards.
The board accepted the town manager's recommendation on an extra-large trash bag pilot, and voted on white paint for Town Hall and a T-Mobile occupancy license pending Town Meeting.
The board voted on a new town manager evaluation form and goals; the outcome was not audible, and one member said they would not support it.
Public comment centered on rumors about moving town offices to the TCP building; no resolution was reached before the board entered executive session on litigation.

why_it_matters: The earth removal permits, the trash bag pilot and the T-Mobile lease touch town revenue, what residents pay for trash bags, and a lease that would need fall Town Meeting approval.
The unresolved debate over moving town offices could lead to building purchase or reuse costs, paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, and to a vote residents may be asked to take.
watch_next: The September 12 workshop, which will be televised in workshop format.
The fall Town Meeting vote on the T-Mobile ten-year lease, and the follow-up hearing on the Montori earth removal permit.

Ours could not hear most votes, while the official records nearly all as passed, so check the audio for those outcomes. The 4-1 tallies on the trash bags and the manager evaluation, and the exact permit terms, need the recording.
